summary: France applies the EU's Schengen visa rules. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, nationals of the third countries listed in Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of those listed in Annex I must hold a visa when crossing the external borders. The EU Visa Code sets the short-stay visa fee at EUR 90, and France-Visas is the official visa website for France. The EU says ETIAS, the travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, is currently not in operation.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for France?
faq.answer: No visa is needed for short stays: the United States is listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. The EU says ETIAS, the travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, is currently not in operation; applying directly through its official website will cost EUR 20.

faq.question: How much does a France Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The EU Visa Code sets the short-stay visa fee at EUR 90, and EUR 45 for children from six years and below 12; children under six are exempt. France-Visas lists the same amounts for a Schengen visa. Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 counts short stays as no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter France?
faq.answer: The EU says ETIAS, the new travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, is currently not in operation and no applications are collected at this point, and that it will announce the start date several months before launch. Applying directly through the official ETIAS website will cost EUR 20.

faq.question: How do I stay in France longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Service-Public says that to enter and stay in France for more than 3 months a foreigner must hold a long-stay visa (type D), granted by the French consular authorities. France-Visas lists the long-stay visa fee as €99, with a reduced rate of €50 for students whose application was examined by a Centre pour les études en France. Service-Public says the VLS-TS long-stay visa counts as a residence permit, and that within 3 months of arriving in France you must validate it and pay a tax on top of the visa fee.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for France?
faq.answer: Yes. Service-Public lists, among the conditions a foreigner must all meet when crossing the border, insurance covering medical and hospital costs for care you might receive in France, with minimum cover of €30,000. The EU Visa Code requires Schengen visa applicants to hold travel medical insurance valid throughout the Member States for the entire intended stay, with minimum coverage of EUR 30,000.
